paper.title_en: LH$μ$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
paper.abstract_en: The concept of the LH$μ$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising $μp$ collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold $μ^+$ beams as proposed for $μ$TRISTAN. For the latter, a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.
